newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares may gain further.
newsitem.headline: KL shares may gain further.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur shares may extend their run-up, particularly among the secondary counters, following Wednesday's recovery from the selloff sparked by U.S. missile attacks on Iraq.

"We may go up another half a percentage point, but not significantly (higher)," said one institutional dealer with a local firm. "I think we're still capped at 1,120 (on the Composite Index) for the short-term."
Overnight, the Dow rose 8.51 points despite weak bond prices. On Wednesday, the Composite Index ended up 12.10 points or 1.11 percent to 1,105.42. It fell 12.88 points on Tuesday.
Speculative interest lofted the Second Board index up 19.43 points to 542.00 on Wednesday.
Regionally, Tokyo stocks were firmer in early trade Thursday, while Taiwan shares are expected to consolidate. In Singapore, stock prices may move sideways to firm.

Dealers said investors are waiting for the release on Friday of U.S. August employment data. A Reuter survey puts payrolls at up 244,000 versus a 193,000 gain in July and the unemployment rate at 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent.
Several recent strong economic reports have raised jitters over possible higher U.S. interest rates.
